$schema.description: Schema is the URL of the format's JSON Schema (package schema), for editors and validators. Captures from before it was added lack it.

id_databases.description: IDDatabases records, per ID database, the source its names came from (e.g. "pci": "/usr/share/hwdata/pci.ids (2026-09-03) + overrides").

tool.description: Tool is the program that wrote the capture.

captured_at.description: CapturedAt is when the capture was taken (RFC 3339).

privileged.description: Privileged is true when the capture ran as root, so the SMBIOS memory list, most serial numbers and drive health could be read. Memory modules' SPD (serials included) is often readable without root.

redacted.description: Redacted is true when what ties the capture to one machine or person was removed (--redact): serial numbers, UUIDs, WWNs, MAC and Bluetooth addresses, the hostname, the asset tag, partition labels and personal mount points. Manufacture dates are kept to the month.

version.description: os-release VERSION_ID; absent on rolling releases

arch.description: the machine, as uname -m, e.g. x86_64

secure_boot.description: SecureBoot is the firmware's Secure Boot state; absent when not UEFI or not readable.

os.description: OS is the running operating system, from os-release and the kernel.

manufacture_date.description: ManufactureDate is ISO 8601 at the precision the part reports: "2020", "2020-03", "2020-W10" or "2020-03-14".

identity.description: Identity is the machine's (SMBIOS type 1): model is the product name, part_number the SKU.

family.description: the product family, as the firmware names it

name.description: Name says which firmware of a part this is, where a part has several (a GPU's firmware_components: "GuC", "HuC", "GuC (gt1)").

date.description: the build date, as the firmware states it

release.description: Release is a second version number the firmware reports: the BIOS release ("5.17"), or a Bluetooth controller's HCI revision.

source.description: Source says where the version was read: dmi, microcode, nvme, scsi (SATA, SAS and USB disks), mmc, ethtool, usb, vbios (amdgpu, and the NVIDIA driver's /proc file), mei, udev (a TPM 2.0, from systemd's tpm2_id), tpm (a TPM 2.0 asked under --full), caps (a TPM 1.2), debugfs (Intel GuC and HuC, under --full), amdgpu (an AMD GPU's blocks), hci (a Bluetooth controller: version is the LMP subversion, release the HCI revision).

instance_ids.description: InstanceIDs are the IDs fwupd knows this part by, each with the GUID LVFS releases name it with (ADR 0012): derived from the part's own IDs, so a capture can be compared with a firmware catalogue offline.

me_firmware.description: MEFirmware is the Intel Management Engine (CSME) firmware, and ECFirmware the embedded controller's: separate controllers with their own firmware.

ec_firmware.description: Firmware is the firmware a part runs, as the part or its driver reports it. A part that has firmware always has this block (ADR 0008): with a version and its source, or, when the version can't be read, Status "unknown" and the Reason, never silently absent.

lowest_supported_fw_version.description: LowestSupportedFWVersion is the oldest version the firmware accepts as an update.

entries.description: ESRTEntry is one updatable firmware. Versions are the 32-bit numbers the firmware reports, before any vendor format is applied.

status.description: "unknown" when the entries couldn't be read

esrt.description: ESRT is the UEFI firmware's EFI System Resource Table: the firmware it can update by capsule, each by the GUID LVFS releases name. Absent without UEFI or an ESRT.

system.description: System is the machine as a whole; its firmware is the BIOS/UEFI.

manufacture_date.description: ManufactureDate is ISO 8601 at the precision the part reports: "2020", "2020-03", "2020-W10" or "2020-03-14".

asset_tag.description: the owner's inventory tag, if set

width.description: electrical width, e.g. "x4"; the type's xN is the physical one

address.description: Address is the PCI address the firmware gives for the slot, as written; "" when it gives none.

slots.description: Slots and OnboardDevices are the firmware's SMBIOS tables (types 9 and 41, root only) as it states them. Their addresses can be wrong: compare them with the PCI topology before trusting them.

enabled.description: whether the firmware has it enabled

instance.description: tells devices of one type apart

onboard_devices.description: OnboardDevice is a device the firmware says is soldered onto the board (SMBIOS type 41).

manufacture_date.description: ManufactureDate is ISO 8601 at the precision the part reports: "2020", "2020-03", "2020-W10" or "2020-03-14".

identity.description: vendor = CPUID vendor string, model = brand string

family.description: Family, ModelID and Stepping are the x86 signature, as the kernel reports it (decimal).

codename.description: Codename and Microarchitecture come from the cpu ID database.

sockets.description: physical processor packages the kernel sees

mounting.description: Mounting is "socket", "slot" (a cartridge) or "onboard" (soldered) when the package's name says so.

populated.description: whether a processor is in it

packages.description: Packages is what the firmware says each processor socket takes (SMBIOS type 4, root only), and whether that package is socketed or soldered.

governor.description: Governor is cpufreq's scaling governor (CPU 0's), e.g. powersave.

instances.description: how many copies exist (e.g. one L2 per core)

caches.description: Cache is one level and type of CPU cache.

date.description: the build date, as the firmware states it

module.description: the kernel module providing it, if not built in

version.description: Version is the module's own version; in-tree modules usually have none, and match the kernel.

srcversion.description: SrcVersion is the checksum of the module's source (modinfo srcversion), which tells two builds of one version apart.

builtin.description: built into the kernel, not a loadable module

in_tree.description: InTree is false for a module built outside the kernel tree (taint flag O). Absent when the taint flags can't be read, as for Proprietary and Unsigned.

proprietary.description: Proprietary is true for a module under a non-GPL-compatible licence (taint flag P).

unsigned.description: Unsigned is true for a module loaded without a valid signature (taint flag E), set only when the kernel exposes module.sig_enforce; unpatched kernels before 5.13 can expose it without module signing.

reasons.description: why the status isn't ok, one line each

life_used_percent.description: LifeUsedPercent and LifeRemainingPercent come only from the part's own wear indicator (NVMe percentage used, SSD endurance, battery capacity versus design, measured on its 100% to 80% range). Used may exceed 100; remaining stops at 0.

method.description: how Value was computed, in words

estimate.description: Estimate is a derived figure; Method says how it was computed.

metrics.description: Metrics are measurements by name (the Metric* constants; the schema lists them as examples), in the unit the name ends with, or a count. Newer builds may add names.

health.description: Health is from the thermal throttling counters.

cpu.description: CPU is the machine's processors, taken together.

total_bytes.description: TotalBytes is what the kernel can use (MemTotal), a little less than InstalledBytes because firmware and the kernel reserve some.

installed_bytes.description: InstalledBytes is the modules' total, from SMBIOS (root only), as are MaxCapacityBytes, Slots and ECC.

max_capacity_bytes.description: the most the board takes, as the firmware states

ecc.description: the error correction in use, e.g. None, Single-bit ECC

locator.description: the slot's label, e.g. DIMM A1

populated.description: Populated is whether a module is in the slot; absent when the firmware doesn't say.

slot_usage.description: SlotUsage lists every memory slot the firmware describes (SMBIOS type 17, root only), used or empty. Absent means not read, never "no slots"; it is never inferred from the usable memory.

locator.description: Locator is the slot's label, e.g. DIMM A1; for a module read from SPD alone, "SPD" and its I2C device, e.g. "SPD 0-0050".

configured_speed_mts.description: the speed it runs at, in MT/s

configured_voltage_mv.description: the voltage it runs at, in millivolts

manufacture_date.description: ManufactureDate is ISO 8601 at the precision the part reports: "2020", "2020-03", "2020-W10" or "2020-03-14".

identity.description: Identity.Vendor is decoded from a JEDEC code when the firmware gives one; ManufacturerRaw then keeps the firmware's string, e.g. "Unknown - [0xF785]".

dram_vendor_id.description: DRAMVendorID is the memory chips' maker, which can differ from the module's (from SPD): its JEDEC code, and DRAMVendor the name resolve fills in.

package.description: Package is, for kind cpu, the processor's package as the firmware names it ("Socket LGA1151", root only).

confidence.description: Confidence is high (the evidence names this part), medium (it fits only one way, but the firmware's own link is broken or the type is ambiguous), or absent for unknown.

evidence.description: what showed it, one finding each

reason.description: Reason says why it's unknown, or what lowered the confidence.

mounting.description: Mounting is whether a part is soldered on or removable, with what showed it.

modules.description: MemoryModule is one installed memory module, from SMBIOS (root only) or, without it, the module's SPD.

memory.description: Memory is the machine's RAM: what the kernel sees, and the modules.

wwn.description: the World Wide Name, a unique ID

type.description: Type is nvme, ssd, hdd, flash, virtual, optical or unknown; it is the authority on whether a disk spins.

rotational.description: Rotational is the kernel's flag. false also means it couldn't be read, so it's not evidence of an SSD: read type.

partuuid.description: the partition table entry's UUID (lsblk PARTUUID)

mount_point.description: MountPoint is where it's mounted; --redact keeps only system ones such as / and /boot.

partitions.description: Partition is one partition of a disk.

clocks.description: GPUClocks is the graphics core's hardware clock range, and its measured clock when the capture was taken: a moment's value, not a sustained one. Present only when the driver exposes them without root.

boot_vga.description: BootVGA is the kernel's boot_vga flag: the GPU the firmware showed the boot screen on. false also means it couldn't be read.

speed.description: as the kernel writes it, e.g. "16.0 GT/s PCIe"

max_width.description: the most lanes the device supports

pcie_link.description: PCIeLink is a PCI Express link's state when captured, and the most the device supports. A link below that may be saving power, or be held back by the slot.

reasons.description: why the status isn't ok, one line each

life_used_percent.description: LifeUsedPercent and LifeRemainingPercent come only from the part's own wear indicator (NVMe percentage used, SSD endurance, battery capacity versus design, measured on its 100% to 80% range). Used may exceed 100; remaining stops at 0.

method.description: how Value was computed, in words

estimate.description: Estimate is a derived figure; Method says how it was computed.

metrics.description: Metrics are measurements by name (the Metric* constants; the schema lists them as examples), in the unit the name ends with, or a count. Newer builds may add names.

health.description: Health describes a part's condition and wear.

batteries.description: Battery is one of the machine's own batteries (power_supply); peripherals' batteries are left out.

spec_version_major.description: SpecVersionMajor is the TCG specification major version the TPM implements (1 or 2).

name.description: Name says which firmware of a part this is, where a part has several (a GPU's firmware_components: "GuC", "HuC", "GuC (gt1)").

date.description: the build date, as the firmware states it

release.description: Release is a second version number the firmware reports: the BIOS release ("5.17"), or a Bluetooth controller's HCI revision.

source.description: Source says where the version was read: dmi, microcode, nvme, scsi (SATA, SAS and USB disks), mmc, ethtool, usb, vbios (amdgpu, and the NVIDIA driver's /proc file), mei, udev (a TPM 2.0, from systemd's tpm2_id), tpm (a TPM 2.0 asked under --full), caps (a TPM 1.2), debugfs (Intel GuC and HuC, under --full), amdgpu (an AMD GPU's blocks), hci (a Bluetooth controller: version is the LMP subversion, release the HCI revision).

tpm.description: TPM is the machine's Trusted Platform Module.

batt_status.description: BattStatus is the driver's batt_status in /proc/driver/rtc: okay or dead, rtc-cmos's reading of the clock chip's "valid RAM and time" bit (Register D, VRT). Only dead is evidence, of a failed cell. okay isn't evidence of a good one: Intel's chipsets hardwire VRT to 1, so they report okay whatever the cell's state. Neither says how much charge is left.

rtc.description: RTC is the real-time clock: what its driver says about the coin cell that keeps it running while the machine is unplugged (#113).

device.description: the address of the device it measures

label.description: the chip's label, or the sensor's name (temp1)

readings.description: SensorReading is one sensor's value when captured.

sensors.description: Sensor is one hardware monitoring chip (hwmon) and its readings.

parent.description: Parent is the bridge or root port the device sits behind, from the kernel's device path (for a root port behind Intel VMD, the VMD controller). Absent on a platform root bus, and when the path can't be resolved, which the capture warns about.

subsystem_vendor_id.description: the card or board maker's vendor ID

subsystem_device_id.description: that maker's ID for the product

class_code.description: ClassCode is the class, subclass and programming interface, 6 hex digits, e.g. 030000 (VGA).

class.description: the class code's name, e.g. "VGA compatible controller"

iommu_group.description: the IOMMU group's number; absent without an IOMMU

speed.description: as the kernel writes it, e.g. "16.0 GT/s PCIe"

max_width.description: the most lanes the device supports

pcie_link.description: PCIeLink is a PCI Express link's state when captured, and the most the device supports. A link below that may be saving power, or be held back by the slot.

label.description: Label is the firmware's name for the device (sysfs label), and LabelSource where the kernel got it: "smbios" (type 41, an onboard device) or "acpi" (a _DSM name, which says nothing about mounting).

kind.description: Kind is onboard (soldered), socket, slot, cpu (part of the processor: it changes only with the CPU), or unknown.

slot.description: Slot names the slot as the firmware does ("Slot2 / M2 WLAN/BT"); SlotType is its type ("PCI Express Gen 3 x1"). When several slots could hold the part, SlotType is set and Slot isn't.

package.description: Package is, for kind cpu, the processor's package as the firmware names it ("Socket LGA1151", root only).

confidence.description: Confidence is high (the evidence names this part), medium (it fits only one way, but the firmware's own link is broken or the type is ambiguous), or absent for unknown.

evidence.description: what showed it, one finding each

reason.description: Reason says why it's unknown, or what lowered the confidence.

mounting.description: Mounting says whether the device is soldered on or sits in a slot, for storage, network, display, multimedia and wireless devices.
